h: Time, tides and a tunnel under the Thames
p: At the Royal Observatory, keep an eye on the red time ball on top of Flamsteed House. It drops every day at 1pm, a signal that once allowed ships on the Thames to set their clocks. By the gate, the Shepherd Gate Clock shows Greenwich Mean Time on a 24-hour dial. Inside, John Harrison's marine timekeepers, H1 to H4, tell the story of how the problem of finding longitude at sea was finally solved.
The Peter Harrison Planetarium runs shows that suit everyone from little ones to serious stargazers, so it's worth booking a slot in advance.

Right by the Cutty Sark, the Greenwich Foot Tunnel runs under the Thames to the Isle of Dogs. It's free, a bit spooky and great fun for kids. The Old Royal Naval College, next to the Maritime Museum, is home to the Painted Hall, a breathtaking baroque ceiling that's often called the UK's Sistine Chapel.
Plan for lots of walking and a few hills. Greenwich Park is a lovely place for a picnic, so pack one if the weather is kind.

Hungry? Greenwich Market's street food stalls are a cracking shout, with something for every fussy eater in the family. Then grab a spot on the grass, look out over the river and try to work out which hemisphere you're sitting in.
